## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

- define observable signals for synchronous and asynchronous workflows
- connect service objectives to metrics and alerts
- design a failure drill with a verifiable recovery condition
- compare the current architecture with credible alternatives

## Observability answers questions

Logs explain individual events, metrics reveal trends, and traces connect work
across boundaries. Each signal needs stable identifiers.

Useful correlation fields include rental ID, event ID, event type and version,
consumer name, service version, and request trace ID.

## Signals for the event path

| Question | Signal |
|---|---|
| Is publication keeping up? | Published List depth and oldest age |
| Is routing blocked? | Routing List depth and error count |
| Is a consumer behind? | Ready and processing depth per consumer |
| Are duplicates increasing? | Idempotence-hit counter |
| Are messages invalid? | Validation and dead-letter counts |

Queue depth without message age can hide a small but permanently stuck queue.

## Service objectives

An objective should describe user-visible behavior and a time window.

Example: 99 percent of accepted auction results produce an insurance offer
within 10 seconds over a rolling 30-day window.

The associated indicator needs timestamps at publication and successful
consumer commit. Infrastructure uptime alone cannot measure this outcome.

## Failure drills

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Hypothesis[Recovery hypothesis] --> Inject[Controlled failure]
    Inject --> Observe[Collect evidence]
    Observe --> Recover[Verify recovery]
    Recover --> Improve[Record corrective action]
```

A drill has a limited blast radius, an abort condition, an owner, and a clear
definition of recovered service.

## Architecture scorecard

| Quality | Current strength | Current limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Learnability | Lists expose delivery steps | More custom code than a broker abstraction |
| Decoupling | Stable ingress and subscriptions | Router fan-out can duplicate |
| Recoverability | Processing Lists retain work | Dead-letter policy remains incomplete |
| Evolvability | Versioned event contracts | Contract retirement needs governance |
| Query flexibility | PostgreSQL supports business queries | No separate CQRS projection yet |

Trade-offs require workload evidence rather than technology preference.

## Next experimental increments

Redis Streams will run beside Lists and compare consumer groups, pending
entries, replay, and retention. CQRS will then add a separate read projection
and make freshness visible to the user.

The existing Lists path stays available as the baseline. See
[`training/roadmap.qmd`](../../roadmap.qmd) for entry criteria.

## Module investigation

1. Define one user objective for auction and insurance processing.
2. Map every objective to logs, metrics, or traces.
3. Run one bounded failure drill.
4. Recommend the next architecture increment from observed evidence.
